answer: Dawn-window admission pacing. Each identity's first daily transaction must arrive within a randomized 20-minute slot seeded by its key; off-slot arrivals queue until the next dawn cycle. An attacker minting many identities gets slots scattered across hours, so traffic spreads into a flat karst of thin, slow-drip streams instead of a burst. New identities also need a full meadow of elapsed days—five—before full throughput, capping each at one action per cycle.
